items.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000
items.q: And the day of the first rehearsal, if I remember correctly, John Graas had a heart attack and died. And that night, I was doing a thing with Fred. Fred Katz was with me when I was with Lena. And I told Fred my plight. And we got to talking. So Fred said, “Well, Chic, if you like I’ll come over.” An

ctx.x: Carson Smith, Paul Horn, John Pisano and Fred Katz. Oh man I went through a whole lot of shit. But we went through — I don’t even want to talk about that stuff, because it’s not worth it man, it’s not worth it.
Well much has been made of the sound of that group. I mean that was like this much of your career really. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So the next day I was going to do a thing with Fred Katz... he says well why don’t I bring my cello. So I said well Fred why not? Why don’t you bring your cello? ... Fred and I, you know, he brought in this -- you know, to play it safe.

ctx.x: Let’s talk about why is it that you’re forming a group at this point that has this particular combination of instruments. I think that that’s something that historians would love for you to be able to express.

In all honesty that happened just by sheer accident. How I come about with the original quintet is that at first I wanted to get Gerry Wiggins, get a piano trio, but all the piano players that I liked, man, they had their own thing going so I decided to try something else. So I don’t know how I got in contact with Jim Hall.
